To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ratios of the neutron ( n ) and proton ( p ) transition matrix elements ( TMEs) ( M n / TME n and M p / TME p ) for 0 + to 2 + transitions have been measured in inelastic hadron ( p and d ) scattering from 12 C and 16 O.

the ratios of neutron to proton transition matrix elements, M n / M ρ, for 0 + to 2 + transitions, are in general agreement between inelastic hadron and electromagnetic scattering and that they show a systematic trend that is consistent with schematic-model calculations.

the ratios of the neutron to proton transition matrix elements for 0 + ( J = 0 ) → 2 + ( J =2 ) transitions in SCS nuclei have a general consistency from inelastic hadron to electromagnetic transition rates to an accuracy ≈ 15% and show a general trend that the neutron transition matrix elements are larger than the collective model result ( N / Z ) in nuclei with neutron valence shells and smaller than the collective model in nuclei with proton valence shells.

the ratios are generally in agreement with the collective-model predictions for nuclei with N and Z ≤ 14 and that core-polarization corrections are needed for heavier SCS nuclei and that these corrections are larger for proton transitions than for neutron transitions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
hadron scattering can be a useful tool for the study of transition matrix elements, especially for the case of 0 + →2 + transitions.
hadron scattering can be used to determine the ratios of neutron and proton transition amplitudes in SCS nuclei.
hadron scattering can be used to study nuclear structure in the same way that electromagnetic transition rates are used.
